Likewise His saying: ﴿He said: Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three nights, except by signs﴾ [Al 'Imran: 41]. God made for him a sign of what he was given glad tidings of, which is his being prevented from speech, while he was not prevented from gesture, as evidenced by His saying: (p-408) ﴿except by signs﴾, and His saying: ﴿So he revealed to them that they should glorify [God] morning and evening﴾ [Maryam: 11]. This indicates that gesture is not like speech. But the first verse is more explicit in indicating that gesture is not like the word, because the second verse admits the possibility that gesture is like speech; for His exception ﴿except by signs﴾ from His saying ﴿that you will not speak to people﴾ is understood to mean that the sign, which is gesture, is a kind of speech from which it is excepted, since the basic principle of exception is connection. And God, exalted is He, knows best.

When you know the evidences of the two groups concerning gesture, whether it is like the word or not, know that scholars differ about comprehensible gesture, whether it takes the place of the word or not; and we will mention here, God willing, some sentences of the statements of the people of knowledge on this, and what its preponderance appears to be by evidence.

Ibn Hajar, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said in Fath al-Bari at the end of the chapter on gesture in divorce and matters, the following text: The scholars have differed about comprehensible gesture. As for rights of God, they said: it suffices, even from one able to speak. As for rights of human beings, such as contracts, acknowledgment, bequest and the like, scholars have differed concerning one whose tongue is tied. Third, from Abu Hanifa: if he is despaired of speaking; and from some Hanbalis: if it is connected to death; and al-Tahawi preferred it; and from al-Awza'i: if speech preceded it; and it is reported from Makhul: if he says "So-and-so is free," then he is silenced, and it is said to him: "And so-and-so?" and he gestures, it is valid. As for one able to speak, his gesture does not stand in place of his speech according to the majority; and it has been disputed whether it stands in place of intention, as when he divorces his wife and it is said to him: "How many pronouncements?" and he points with his finger. End of quotation from him.

Al-Bukhari said at the beginning of the chapter on li'an, the following text: If the mute slanders his wife by writing or by a known gesture or sign, then he is like one who speaks; for the Prophet (ﷺ) permitted gesture in the obligatory matters. This is the saying of some people of the Hijaz and scholars. God said: ﴿So she pointed to him; they said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ Qatadah said: ﴿except by signs﴾ means gesture. Some people said: there is no hadd nor li'an; then he claimed that if he divorces by writing, gesture or sign, it is permitted, and there is no difference between divorce and slander. If he says: slander cannot occur except by speech, it is said to him: likewise divorce is not permitted except by speech, otherwise divorce and slander are void; and likewise manumission; and likewise the deaf can perform li'an. Al-Sha'bi and Qatadah said: if he says "You are divorced" and gestures with his fingers, he is separated by his gesture. Ibrahim said: if the mute writes divorce with his hand, it binds him. Hammad said: if the mute and deaf nod with the head, it is valid. End of the point of the purpose of al-Bukhari's words, may Allah have mercy on him.

(p-409) The positions of the four Imams are close on this question, though among them there is difference in some of its branches.

The school of Malik, may God have mercy on him, holds that an understandable gesture takes the place of speech. Khalil ibn Ishaq said in his *Mukhtasar*, in which he stated in its introduction what the school issues as legal opinion, meaning in the school of Malik: "Speech is with the formula by which divorce takes effect, and it is binding by an understandable gesture." That is, divorce is binding by an understandable gesture absolutely, whether from a mute person or a speaking one.

His commentator al-Mawwaq, may God have mercy on him, said, quoting the *Mudawwana*: "What is known from a mute person, by gesture or in writing, of divorce, khul' (divorce at the wife's request), manumission, marriage, sale, purchase, or slander, the ruling of one who speaks applies to him." Al-Baji narrated: "The gesture of a sound person with divorce, with his head or his hand, is like his words, based on the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿That you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 41]." The end of what is from him. This narration of al-Baji is what the people of the school act upon.

The school of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, holds that the gesture of a mute person takes the place of the speech of one who speaks in his dispositions, such as his manumission and divorce, his sale and purchase, and similar matters. As for a sound person, his gesture is not accepted by him, because he is able to speak. The gesture of a mute person in accusing his wife of adultery does not, in his view, entail the hadd punishment (the prescribed punishment) or li'an (the oath of mutual cursing between spouses), because the hudud are averted by doubts, and the absence of explicit speech is a doubt in his view. This is because a gesture may convey what the one gesturing does not intend. Also, the oaths of li'an have required formulas that must be said and cannot be made by gesture. Likewise, in his view, if the wife accused is mute, there is no hadd and no li'an, because it is possible that if she spoke she would confirm him, and because she cannot produce the words of the oaths prescribed in the verse of li'an. Likewise, in his view, slander is not valid from a mute person, because the hudud are averted by doubts.

Some scholars of the Hanafis said: Analogy (qiyas) prevents recognizing the gesture of a mute person, because it is not understood in every respect as speech is. They permitted acting on the gesture of a mute person in matters other than li'an and slander by way of istihsan (juristic preference), while analogy prohibits it absolutely. The school of al-Shafi'i in this question is to recognize the gesture of a mute person in li'an and other matters, and not to recognize the gesture of a sound person.

As for the school of Imam Ahmad, the apparent statement of Ahmad, may God Most High have mercy on him, is that there is no li'an if one of the spouses is mute, as we mentioned its rationale in the school of Abu Hanifa. Qadi Abu al-Khattab said: If the gesture of a mute person is understood, he is like one who speaks in his slander and li'an. As for the divorce of a mute person, his marriage, and similar matters, the gesture is like speech in the school of Imam Ahmad. As for a sound person, his gesture with divorce and the like is not accepted by him.

This is the summary of the statements of the imams and others among the jurists of the regions on this question, and you have seen what came concerning it of the evidences from the Book and the Sunnah.

The one who wrote this, may God pardon him and forgive him, says: What appears to me to be preponderant in the question is this: if the gesture indicates the meaning with a clear indication, such that there is no doubt about the intended meaning with it, then it takes the place of speech absolutely, unless the specific wording has a particular importance intended by the Lawgiver. If it has such importance, the gesture does not take its place, like the oaths of li'an, since God specified them in a particular form. So the apparent view is that a gesture does not take their place, and likewise all words that are required in worship, for a gesture does not suffice for them. And God, Exalted is He, knows best.

As for His saying, in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, meaning, according to the majority, abstention from speech. Sawm (fasting) in the language means abstention, and from it is the saying of Nabigha Dhubyani:

Horses that abstain, and horses that do not abstain, under the dust, and others chewing the bits.

So his saying "horses that abstain" means restraining from running, and it was said also from fodder. "And horses that do not abstain" means not restraining from what was mentioned.

And the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

As if the Pleiades were hung in their station by ropes of flax to a hard rock.

So his saying "in their station" means the place of their abstention, that is, their holding still from motion. This view is the correct meaning of the verse, that the intended sawm is abstention from speech, as evidenced by His saying after it: ﴿So I will not speak today to any human being﴾. This is the view of most of the people of knowledge. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*, in the chapter on li'an: "It has been established from the hadith of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Anas ibn Malik that the meaning of His saying, ﴿Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast﴾, is silence (samt). It was recorded by al-Tabarani and others." End of quotation. Some scholars said: the intended sawm in the verse is the known legal fast mentioned in His saying: ﴿Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you﴾ [al-Baqara: 183]. On this view, the meaning is that when they fasted in their law, speech was forbidden to them just as food was forbidden. But the correct meaning of the verse is the first, and on it, this vow, that she would not speak to any human today, was permissible in their law. As for the law that our Prophet (ﷺ) brought, that vow is not permissible, and fulfilling it is not obligatory.

Al-Bukhari said in his *Sahih*: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "While the Prophet (ﷺ) was delivering a sermon, he saw a man standing, and he asked about him. They said: 'He is Abu Isra'il, who vowed to stand and not sit, not seek shade, not speak, and to fast.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Order him to speak, to seek shade, to sit, and to complete his fast.'" 'Abd al-Wahhab said: Ayyub narrated to us from Ikrimah, from the Prophet (ﷺ). End of quotation.

Ibn Hajar said in *al-Fath*, in discussing this hadith: "In its narration is that silence from what is permissible is not part of obedience to God. Abu Dawud recorded from the hadith of 'Ali: 'Nor is silence of a day until night.'" It preceded in the *Sirah* that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said that this, meaning silence, is from the practice of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic ignorance). In it is that everything by which a person is harmed, even ultimately, which has not been prescribed by a book or sunnah as legislated, such as walking barefoot or sitting in the sun, is not part of obedience to God, and so a vow is not concluded by it. For the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered Abu Isra'il to complete the fast only, and this is interpreted as his knowing it would not be hard for him, and he ordered him to sit, speak, and seek shade." Al-Qurtubi said: "In the story of Abu Isra'il: this is the clearest proof for the majority that there is no expiation (kaffarah) obligatory upon one who vows an act of disobedience or something in which there is no obedience." Malik said when he mentioned it: "I have not heard that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered him to make expiation." End of the words of the author of *Fath al-Bari*.

Al-Zamakhshari, in his commentary on this noble verse which we are discussing, said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade fasting in silence." Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shaf fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf*: "I have not seen it in this form. 'Abd al-Razzaq recorded from the hadith of Jabir with the wording: 'Nor is silence of a day until night.' In its chain is Hizam ibn 'Uthman, who is weak. Abu Dawud has a similar wording from the hadith of 'Ali." It was mentioned earlier in the tafsir of Surat al-Nisa'.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿And if you see﴾ (fa-imma taraynna), its meaning is: if you see any human being. The word *imma* is composed of *in* (the conditional particle "if") and *ma* (an added particle to emphasize the condition). The original form is *tara'īna*, on the pattern of *taf'alīna*. The letter *ya'* which is the final radical of the root moved and the letter before it was open, so it had to be changed to an *alif*, and it became *tar'ayna*. The hamzah was deleted and its vowel moved to the *ra'*, because the classical language, which is the more common in Arab speech, deletes the hamzah of *ra'a* (to see) in the imperfect and imperative, and moves its vowel to the *ra'*, so it became *taraynna*. Then two sukun (unvowelled consonants) met, so the first, the *alif*, was deleted, and it became *tarayna*. The heavy energetic nun (nun al-tawkid al-thaqilah) was then attached to it, and the nun of the nominative was deleted because of it, as well as because of the jussive particle *in* (the conditional), since each of them alone requires the deletion of the nun of the nominative. So it became *taraynna*. Then two sukun met: the *ya'* with sukun and the first nun with sukun from the doubled energetic nun, since every doubled letter is two letters. So the *ya'* was vowelled with a vowel suited to it, which is the kasrah, and it became *taraynna*. This was indicated by Ibn Malik in the *Khulasah* with his saying:

Delete it from the nominative of these two, and in the waw and the ya' a matching vowel, follow it. Like *ikhshayna* (fear!), O Hind, with kasrah; and *ya qawmi ikhshawna* (O my people, fear!) with damma; and measure similarly.

What we mentioned, that the hamzah of *ra'a* is deleted in the imperfect and imperative, is the regular analogical rule in Arabic speech, while keeping it in its original form is also attested. From it is the saying of Suraqah ibn Mirdas al-Bariqi al-Asghar:

Let my eyes see what you do not see; we are both aware of the falsehoods.

And the saying of al-A'lam ibn Jaradah al-Sa'di, or a poet of Taym al-Rabab:

Did you not see what I encountered while time was squeezing? Whoever makes himself patient with time will see and hear.

And the saying of another:

I yearn when I see the mountains of Najd, and I do not see a path to Najd.

The energetic nun after *imma* in the imperfect verb is obligatory according to some scholars of Arabic grammar. Among those who held that it is obligatory after *imma*, as in His saying here: ﴿And if you see any human being﴾, are al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj. The view of Sibawayh, al-Farisi, and a group is that the energetic nun in the imperfect verb after *imma* is not obligatory. Its evidence is the frequency of its occurrence in Arabic poetry, such as the saying of al-A'sha, Maymun ibn Qays:

If you see me, and I still have locks of hair, then the vicissitudes have worn them away.

And the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah:

If you see me today, having become safe, then I am not more alive than Kilab and Ja'far.

And the saying of al-Shanfara:

If you see me like the daughter of the sand, slender, upon delicacy, I go barefoot and do not wear sandals.

And the saying of al-Afwah al-Awdi:

If you see my head, which the harshness of a time of reversal and despair has marked.

And the saying of another:

Tumadir claimed that if I die, my friends' sons among the young will lead my friendship.

And the saying of another:

O companion, if you find me without a friend, abandoning friends is not my nature.

Examples like these are numerous in Arabic poetry.

Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj say that the omission of the nun in the aforementioned verses and similar ones is only for the necessity of poetry. Those who disagree with them, such as Sibawayh and al-Farisi, deny that it is for necessity, and say that it is permissible absolutely. And God knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly come with a strange thing. O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste."﴾

When Mary was reassured by the extraordinary signs she had witnessed, which were mentioned just before, she brought him, meaning Jesus, to her people, carrying him, without being ashamed or concerned about what they would say. So they said to her: ﴿O Mary, you have certainly come with a strange thing﴾ [Maryam: 27]. Mujahid, Qatadah and others said: "fariyyan" means "great." Sa'id ibn Mas'adah said: "fariyyan" means "fabricated, invented." Abu 'Ubaydah and al-Akhfash said: "fariyyan" means "wondrous, rare."

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: What is understood from the Qur'anic verses is that their intention in saying ﴿you have certainly come with a strange thing﴾ is a great abomination. This is because "al-fariyy" is a form (fa'il) derived from "al-firyah" (slander, fabrication), and by it they meant fornication. This is because the child of fornication is like a fabricated, invented thing, since the fornicatress claims that he belongs to someone who is not his father. What indicates that their intention by "fariyyan" was fornication is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and because of their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander﴾ [al-Nisa': 156]. That great slander, which is their claim that she committed fornication and brought Jesus from that fornication (far be it from her and from him), is what they meant by their saying to her: ﴿you have certainly come with a strange thing﴾. What supports this is His saying after it: ﴿O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste﴾. "Al-baghiyy" means the fornicatress, as has been mentioned before. They meant: your parents were chaste and did not commit immorality, so what is it with you that you commit it!

Among what indicates that the child of fornication is like a fabricated thing is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿nor should they bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 12]. Some scholars said: the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿nor should they bring a slander they have invented between their hands and their feet﴾ is: nor should they bring a child of fornication whom they intend to attribute to a man who is not its father. This is the apparent meaning indicated by the Qur'an regarding the sense of the verse. Every work that its doer perfected is called "fariyy" linguistically. From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet), who is Zurarah ibn Sa'b ibn Dahr:

*And you have fed me a year-old date-stalk (daql),*
*Worm-eaten, maggot-ridden, stony.*

*You used to split (tafrin) with it the great thing (fariyy).*

He means: you used to do with it a great deed. The apparent meaning is that he intends that she fed it to him in a huge, excessive quantity.

As for His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾, it does not mean by it Aaron son of ['Imran], the brother of Musa, as some ignoramuses assume. Rather, it is another righteous man from the Children of Israel named Aaron. The proof that he is not Aaron, the brother of Musa, is what Muslim, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, narrated in his Sahih: "Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-'Anazi narrated to us, and the wording is that of Ibn Numayr. They said: Ibn Idris narrated to us from his father, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Alqamah ibn Wa'il, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, who said: 'When I came to Najran, they asked me and said: "You recite: ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾, and Musa was before 'Isa by such-and-such years." When I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, I asked him about that, and he said: "They used to name themselves after their prophets and the righteous before them."'" End quote. This is the wording of Muslim in the Sahih, and it is evidence that he is a different man from Aaron, the brother of Musa. It is well known that Aaron, the brother of Musa, lived a long time before Mary.

Ibn Hajar said in [al-Kafi al-Shaf fi Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf] regarding al-Zamakhshari's saying: "They only meant Aaron the Prophet," the following: "I have not found it like this except with al-Tha'labi without a chain of transmission. al-Tabari narrated it from al-Suddi as his own saying, and it is not sound. For in Muslim, al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi [it is narrated] from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah who said: 'The Prophet ﷺ sent me to Najran. They said to me: "Have you seen something you recite: ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾, while between Musa and 'Isa there are as many years as Allah willed?" I did not know what to answer them. The Prophet ﷺ said to me: "Why did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the names of their prophets and the righteous before them?"'" Al-Tabari narrated through the route of Ibn Sirin: "I was informed that Ka'b said: Indeed His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾ is not about Aaron the brother of Musa." 'A'ishah said to him: "You have lied." He said to her: "O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet ﷺ said it, then he knows best; otherwise, I find between them six hundred years." End of the words of Ibn Hajar.

The author of [al-Durr al-Manthur] said regarding His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O sister of Aaron﴾: Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Muslim, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Hibban, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in [al-Dala'il] narrated from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent me to Najran" . . . to the end of the hadith as mentioned just above. By this sound hadith, which you have seen these groups narrate, and which we have previously cited in its wording in Muslim's Sahih, you know that the saying of whoever says that the intended one is Aaron the brother of Musa is false, whether it is said that she was his sister, or that by "she is his sister" it is meant that she was of his descendants, as one says to a man: "O brother of Tamim," meaning "O brother of the Banu Tamim," because he is of the descendants of Tamim. From this category is His saying: ﴿and mention the brother of 'Ad﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 21], because Hud was only called "the brother of 'Ad" because he was of their descendants; he is the brother of the Banu 'Ad, and they are what is meant by 'Ad in the verse, because what is meant by it is the tribe, not the ancestor. When you have verified that what is meant by Aaron in the verse is other than Aaron the brother of Musa, know that some scholars said: she had a brother named Aaron. Others say: the Aaron mentioned was a man of her people who was well known for righteousness. On this view, what is meant by her being his sister is that she resembled him in worship and piety. The application of the name "brother" to a counterpart or similar person is well known in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. From the Qur'an is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We show them no sign except that it is greater than its sister﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 48], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed the wasteful were brothers of the devils﴾ [al-Isra': 27], and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿whose brothers aid them in error, then they do not restrain﴾ [al-A'raf: 202]. From Arabic speech is the saying:

*Every brother is parted from by his brother,*
*By the life of your father, except the two Farqads.*

So he made the two Farqads brothers.

The Arabs very often apply the name "brother" to a friend and companion. From its application to a companion is the saying of al-Qulakh ibn Hazn:

*O brother of war, clothing it with its splendor,*
*And not an intruder into the rear-ranks, nor one who is foolish.*

So his saying "brother of war" means its companion.

From it is the saying of al-Ra'i, and it was said to Abu Dhu'ayb:

*On a morning when Su'da appeared to a monk*
*At Dawmah, a stone cairn between them and a pilgrim.*

*He abandoned his religion and was stirred by longing, for she,*
*Despite the distance, is the brothers of consolation, a yearner.*

So his saying "the brothers of consolation" means the companions of patience.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 29:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So she pointed to him﴾.

The meaning of her pointing to him is that they should speak to him, and he would inform them of the reality of the matter. The evidence that this is what she intended by her pointing to him is His saying, exalted is He, after it: ﴿They said, "How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?"﴾ [Maryam: 29]. So the past-tense verb "kāna" (was) carries the meaning of the present-tense verb associated with the present time, as the context indicates. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 30:

The Quranic verses: ﴿He said, "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah. He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet.﴾ ﴿And He has made me blessed wherever I am and has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive.﴾ ﴿And [He has made me] dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a domineering wretch.﴾ ﴿And peace is upon me the day I was born, and the day I will die, and the day I will be raised alive.﴾

(p-416) Allah, glorified and exalted, mentions in this noble verse that the first word Jesus uttered to them while he was an infant in his cradle was that he is the servant of Allah. In this there is the greatest rebuke to the Christians regarding their claim that he is Allah, or the son of Allah, or a god along with Him. This word which Jesus uttered at the beginning of his address to them, Allah, glorified and exalted, related it from him in other places,

• such as His saying: ﴿And the Messiah said, "O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 72],

• and His saying in "Al 'Imran": ﴿Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [Al 'Imran: 51],

• and His saying in "al-Zukhruf": ﴿So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 63-64],

• and His saying here in surah "Maryam": ﴿And indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.﴾ [Maryam: 36],

and His saying: ﴿I did not say to them except what You commanded me: "Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord."﴾, and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿He has given me the Scripture and made me a prophet﴾, the verification of this, Allah willing, is that he expressed in the past tense what will occur in the future, treating the certainty of its occurrence as its occurrence. Its parallels in the Quran are numerous,

• such as His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it.﴾ [al-Nahl: 1],

• and His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.﴾ ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Record will be placed, and the prophets and witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be made between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.﴾ ﴿And every soul will be compensated in full for what it did.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven.﴾ [al-Zumar: 68-71],

• and His saying: ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven.﴾ [al-Zumar: 73].

So these past-tense verbs mentioned in the verses carry the meaning of the future, treating the certainty of their occurrence as their actual occurrence. Their parallels in the Quran are numerous. And what we have mentioned, that the past-tense verbs in His saying ﴿He has given me the Scripture﴾ ... etc., carry the meaning of the future, is the correct view, Allah willing, contrary to those who claimed that he was given prophethood and the Scripture in his childhood, based on the apparent wording. His saying ﴿and made me blessed﴾ means: abundant in blessings, because he knows good and calls to Allah, and heals the blind and the leper and raises the dead by Allah's permission. Al-Zamakhshari said in his tafsir of this verse: ﴿blessed wherever I am﴾, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "beneficial wherever I am." Ibn Hajar said in *al-Kafi al-Shafi*: Abu Nu'aym related it in *al-Hilyah*, in the biography of Yunus ibn 'Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, with this and more. He said: Hushaym alone related it from Yunus, and from him Shu'ayb ibn Muhammad al-Kufi narrated it. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated it through this chain. End of quotation.

His saying in this noble verse ﴿and dutiful to my mother﴾: al-Hawfi and Abu al-Baqa' said it is (p-417) coordinated with His saying: ﴿and made me blessed﴾. Abu Hayyan said in *al-Bahr*: there is a distance in this, due to the separation between the coordinated and the coordinated-to by the clause "has enjoined upon me" and its complement. The better view is that it is in the accusative by an implied verb, i.e., "and made me dutiful to my mother." When he said "to my mother" and did not say "to my parents," it was known that this is a matter from Allah, as al-Qurtubi reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. The meaning of "domineering and wretched" has already been mentioned. Al-Qurtubi, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his tafsir of this verse: "wretched," i.e., deprived of good. Ibn 'Abbas said: disobedient to his parents. It was also said: disobedient to his Lord. It was said: "He did not make me one who abandons His command, so that I would be wretched as Iblis was wretched." End of al-Qurtubi's words.

* *

Note

Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, used this verse as evidence against the Qadariyyah. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this noble verse: Malik ibn Anas, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said regarding this verse: "How severe it is against the people of qadar! 'Isa, peace be upon him, informed of what was decreed concerning his affair and what will happen until he dies." End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 34:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is Jesus, son of Mary, the word of truth about which they dispute﴾. Know that this word has two of the seven recitational variants (qira'at sab'iyyah, the seven canonical readings). Nafi', Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i recited "qawlu al-haqq" [Maryam: 34] with a damma on the lam, while Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim recited ﴿qawla al-haqq﴾ with a fatha (nasb).

The demonstrative in His saying "dhalika" refers to the child mentioned in the verses before this. "Dhalika" is the subject (mubtada'), "Isa" is its predicate (khabar), and "ibnu Maryam" is a qualifier (na't) of "Isa". It has also been said that it is an apposition (badal) of it, and it has been said that it is a predicate following a predicate (khabar ba'da khabar).

His saying ﴿qawla al-haqq﴾, according to the reading with the fatha, is a verbal noun (masdar) emphasizing the content of the sentence. Ibn Malik alluded to this type in his Khulasah (Alfiyyah) with his saying:

"And the second, like 'ibnay anta haqqan sirfa'" 

It has also been said that it is in the accusative of praise (nasb 'ala al-madh). As for the reading of the majority with the raf' (nominative), then "qawlu al-haqq" is the predicate of an omitted subject (mubtada' mahdhuf), i.e., "he" — i.e., his attribution to his mother alone is "the word of truth." This was said by Abu Hayyan. Al-Zamakhshari said: its raf' is either as a predicate following a predicate, or an apposition, or the predicate of an omitted subject.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him and forgive him, says: Know that the word "al-haqq" in His saying here, "qawla al-haqq," has two interpretations among the scholars:

(p-418) The first: the intended meaning of "al-haqq" is the opposite of falsehood, in the sense of truth and certainty, as in His saying: ﴿And your people denied it, though it is the truth﴾. According to this view, the i'rab (grammatical parsing) of "qawla al-haqq" in the reading with the fatha is that it is a verbal noun emphasizing the content of the sentence, as already mentioned, and in the reading with the damma it is the predicate of an omitted subject, as already mentioned. This interpretation is supported by His saying, the Exalted, in "Al 'Imran" in the same narrative: ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Al 'Imran: 60].

The second interpretation: the intended meaning of "al-haqq" in the verse is Allah, Exalted and Majestic, since one of His names is "al-Haqq." As in His saying: ﴿And they know that Allah is the manifest truth﴾ [al-Nur: 25], and His saying: ﴿That is because Allah is the truth﴾ [al-Hajj: 62] and so on. According to this view, the i'rab of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿qawla al-haqq﴾ [Maryam: 34], in the reading with the fatha, is that it is in the accusative of praise, and in the reading with the damma it is an apposition of "Isa" or a predicate. According to this interpretation, "qawla al-haqq" is "Isa," just as Allah named him a word (kalimah) in His saying: ﴿and His word which He conveyed to Maryam﴾ [al-Nisa': 171], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good news of a word from Him, whose name is al-Masih﴾ [Al 'Imran: 45] and so on. "Isa" was named a word only because Allah brought him into existence by His word, which is "Be!", and he was, as He said: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59]. According to this interpretation, "qawl" and "kalimah" have the same meaning in the explanation.

His saying: ﴿about which they dispute﴾, i.e., they doubt. The verb "yamtarun" is from the form ifti'al of "mirya," which means doubt. This doubt that befell the disbelievers is the doubt that Allah forbade the Muslims from, through the tongue of their Prophet, in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with Allah is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he is﴾ and ﴿The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters﴾ [Al 'Imran: 59–60]. This true word, by which Allah clarified the reality of the matter concerning Jesus, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, came after the revelation to our Prophet (ﷺ), when his Lord commanded him to invite whoever disputed with him about Jesus to mutual cursing (mubahalah, the mutual invocation of Allah's curse upon the liars). Then He informed him that what He related to him of the account of Jesus is the true narrative. This is in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So whoever disputes with you about it after knowledge has come to you, say, "Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us earnestly pray and invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars."﴾ ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾ [Al 'Imran: 61–62] and so on. When this was revealed and the Prophet (ﷺ) invited the delegation of Najran to mubahalah, they feared destruction and paid the jizyah (poll tax), as is well known.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for Allah to take any son; glory be to Him. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

Know first that the expression "mā kāna" (it is not) indicates negation. Sometimes this negation, in terms of meaning, indicates reproach and deterrence, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It was not for the people of Medina and the Bedouins around them to remain behind the Messenger of Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 120], and sometimes it indicates incapacity (ta'jiz), as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate with Him?﴾ ﴿Or who created the heavens and the earth and sent down for you water from the sky, and We caused to grow thereby gardens of delight, whose trees you could never have grown?﴾ [al-Naml: 59–60].

Sometimes it indicates transcendence (tanzih), as in His saying here: ﴿It is not for Allah to take any son﴾, which He follows with His saying, "glory be to Him," i.e., exalting Him above taking a son and everything that is not befitting to His perfection and majesty. So His saying "mā kāna li-Llāh" means: it is not valid, nor possible, nor conceivable with respect to Him, may He be exalted, that He should take a son. Glory be to Him and exalted is He far above that. This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it does not befit the Most Merciful that He should take a son﴾ [Maryam: 92]. In this verse there is also a thorough refutation of the Christians who claimed the impossible in their saying "Jesus is the son of Allah." And what He, exalted is He, has here declared Himself free of, namely the alleged son falsely attributed to Him, like Jesus, He has declared Himself free of in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is only the Messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Allah is only one God. Glory be to Him that He should have a son﴾ [al-Nisa': 171]. Verses indicating the like of this are many, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son."﴾ ﴿You have certainly brought a thing monstrous.﴾ ﴿The heavens are almost rent from it, the earth split open, and the mountains fall in ruin﴾ ﴿because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son.﴾ ﴿And it is not befitting for the Most Merciful that He should take a son﴾ [Maryam: 88–91], and other verses besides, as has been fully discussed earlier in Surat al-Kahf.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿When He decrees a matter﴾ [Maryam: 35], i.e., He intends its decree, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [al-Nahl: 40], and His saying: ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. The omission of the verb of intending, because the context indicates it, is common in the Qur'an and in Arabic speech. Among its examples in the Qur'an is His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6], i.e., when you intend to stand for it, and His saying: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾ [al-Nahl: 98], i.e., when you intend to recite the Qur'an, as has been fully discussed earlier.

As for His saying in the verse we are concerned with: ﴿It is not for Allah to take any son﴾, the word "min" (any) has been added before the object to emphasize generality. It has been established in the principles of jurisprudence that an indefinite noun in a negative context, when the word "min" is added before it to emphasize generality, becomes an explicit text in generality. Its addition before an indefinite noun in a negative context for the stated emphasis of generality is consistent in three places: before the subject, as in His saying: ﴿There came not to them any warner﴾ [al-Qasas: 46]; before the object, as in this verse, and as in His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that...﴾ [al-Anbiya': 25]; and before the subject of a nominal sentence, as in His saying: ﴿We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him."﴾

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who disbelieved from the scene of a great day﴾. The most apparent of the opinions regarding the "factions" mentioned in this verse is that they are the groups of the Jews and Christians who differed concerning the matter of Jesus. One group said: he is the son of adultery; another group said: he is the son of Allah; another group said: he is Allah; and another group said: he is a god alongside Allah.

Then Allah threatened those among them who disbelieved with woe for them from the witnessing of the Day of Resurrection. This includes both those who disbelieved by going to the extreme of deficiency concerning Jesus, like the one who said he is the son of adultery, and those who disbelieved by going to the extreme of excess concerning him, like those who said he is Allah or His son. His saying "woe" (wayl) is a word of punishment; it is a verbal noun (maṣdar) with no verb from its own form. Its use as a grammatical subject (ibtida') despite being indefinite (nakirah) is permitted because it carries the sense of supplication (du'a'). The apparent meaning of "mashhad" in the verse is a mimi verbal noun (maṣdar mīmī), meaning: "woe to them from witnessing that day," i.e., from its presence, because of the punishment they will encounter in it. This is contrary to those who claimed that "mashhad" in the verse is a noun of place, meaning: "woe to them from that place in which they witness those terrors and punishment." The first is the apparent meaning and is the correct one, God willing, Exalted is He.

This meaning which he mentioned here he also mentioned in Surat az-Zukhruf in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Jesus came with clear proofs, he said: "I have certainly come to you with wisdom and to make clear to you some of that about which you differ. So fear Allah and obey me. Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him; this is a straight path." So the factions differed among themselves, so woe to those who wronged from the punishment of a painful day﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 63–65]. What is indicated in the two verses, that those who disbelieved by excess or deficiency concerning Jesus, peace be upon him and upon our Prophet, He did not hasten punishment upon them, and that He delays their punishment until the appointed time for it, is indicated in other places, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare in horror﴾ [Ibrahim: 42].

• And His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a limited term﴾ [Hud: 104].

• And His saying: ﴿And if not for a specified term, the punishment would have come to them, and it will surely come to them suddenly while they do not perceive﴾ [Al-Ankabut: 53].

In summary, Allah, Exalted is He, gives respite to the wrongdoer until the time of his punishment, but He does not neglect him. It is established in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Indeed, Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102]. And He, Exalted, said: ﴿And how many a city did I give respite while it was wrongdoing, then I seized it, and to Me is the destination﴾ [Al-Hajj: 48].

His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿So the factions differed among themselves﴾ [Maryam: 37]. Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr (al-Bahr al-Muhit): The meaning of His saying "from among themselves" is that the difference did not come from outside them; rather, they were the ones who differed. End of the relevant point from it.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Hear them and see them, on the Day they come to Us! But the wrongdoers today are in clear error.﴾ His saying: ﴿Hear them and see them﴾ are two forms of exclamation (ṣīghatā taʿajjub). The meaning of the noble verse is that the disbelievers, on the Day of Resurrection, will hear and see the realities that the Messengers informed them of, with a wondrous hearing and seeing, whereas in the abode of the world they were in error and heedlessness, not hearing the truth nor seeing it. This which Allah, exalted is He, has explained in this noble verse, He has explained in other places,

• such as His saying concerning their hearing and seeing on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us, that we may do righteous deeds; indeed, we are certain."﴾ [as-Sajdah: 12],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You were certainly in heedlessness of this, so We have removed from you your covering, and your sight today is sharp.﴾ [Qaf: 22],

• and as His saying concerning their heedlessness in the world and their not seeing or hearing: ﴿The reckoning of the people has drawn near to them, while they are in heedlessness, turning away.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 1],

• and His saying: ﴿They know an outward appearance of the worldly life, while they are, concerning the Hereafter, heedless.﴾ [ar-Rum: 7],

• and His saying: ﴿Deaf, dumb, blind; so they will not return.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 18],

• and His saying: ﴿The example of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing…﴾ [Hud: 24], the verse.

By "the blind and the deaf" is meant the disbelievers, and verses similar to this are many. Know that the exclamatory form, when it is on the pattern "af'il bihi" (how [X] he is!), is a verb according to the majority of scholars. Most of them say it is a past-tense verb that has taken the form of an imperative. Some say it is an imperative verb used to produce the exclamation (inshāʾ at-taʿajjub), and this is the apparent meaning of the form. It is supported by the attachment of the emphatic nūn to it, as in the saying of the poet:

"And one who exchanged, after the departure of the tribe, a little herd; so how worthy he is, because of long poverty, to be [in need] and to be cast down!"

Because the alif in his saying "wa-aḥriyā" is substituted for the light emphatic nūn, in accordance with the statement in the Khulasah (Alfiyyah of Ibn Malik):

"And change it, after a fatḥah, into an alif in pause, as you say in qifanna: qifā."

(p-422) The majority also hold that the other exclamatory form, which is "mā afʿalahu" (how [X] he is!), is a past-tense verb, contrary to a group of the Kufans who say it is a noun, as evidenced by its diminutive in the saying of al-ʿArajī:

"How lovely are the gazelles that have passed by us from among these, between the thorn-trees and the samur-trees!"

They said: diminution occurs only in nouns. Those who disagreed with them replied that its diminution in the verse mentioned is anomalous, to be preserved (as transmitted) and not analogically extended.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe﴾. Al-Hasrah (regret): the utmost remorse and loss over a thing that has passed and cannot be made up. Al-Indhar (warning): notification accompanied by a threat. That is: warn the people of the Day of Resurrection. It was said of it, "the Day of Regret," because of the intensity of the disbelievers' remorse therein over their negligence. The believers may also feel remorse therein over the shortcomings that came from them. Allah, exalted is He, has alluded to this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿And warn them of the Imminent Day, when hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief﴾ [Ghafir: 18], and His saying: ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾ [Saba': 46].

He also alluded to what occurs therein of regret in other places:

• Such as His saying: ﴿Lest a soul should say, "Oh, my regret over what I neglected concerning Allah"﴾ [al-Zumar: 56],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with Allah have certainly lost, until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it"﴾ [al-An'am: 31],

• and His saying: ﴿Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets upon them, and they will not be ones who leave the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 167],

along with other verses. His saying in this noble verse, ﴿while they are in heedlessness﴾, means: in the heedlessness of the worldly life, turning away from the Hereafter. The clause "while they are in heedlessness" is a circumstantial clause (hal), and its governing element (al-'amil) is "warn them": that is, warn them while they are in their state of heedlessness, not believing. This is contrary to those who said that the governing element of the circumstantial clause is His saying before this, "in manifest error." A sound hadith has come that indicates that what is meant by His saying here, "when the matter will have been decided," is: death will be slaughtered.

Al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Sahih: "Chapter on the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret﴾. 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Salih narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Death will be brought in the form of a horned ram, white with black spots. A caller will call out: O people of Paradise! They will crane their necks and look. He will say: Do you recognize this? They will say: Yes, this is death, and all of them have seen it. Then he will call out: O people of the Fire! They will crane their necks and look. He will say: Do you recognize this? They will say: Yes, this is death, and all of them have seen it. Then it will be slaughtered, and he will say: O people of Paradise, eternity, with no death! O people of the Fire, eternity, with no death!' Then he recited: ﴿And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will have been decided, while they are in heedlessness﴾ [Maryam: 39]." And these are in the heedlessness of the worldly life, and they do not believe. End of quotation from Sahih al-Bukhari.

The hadith is famous and agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). The Prophet's (ﷺ) recitation of the verse after mentioning the slaughter of death indicates that what is meant by His saying, "when the matter will have been decided," is: death will be slaughtered. Other opinions regarding its meaning exist besides this, which we have omitted because of the indication of the sound hadith to the meaning we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We shall inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned.﴾ The meaning of His saying, majestic and exalted is He, in this verse, that He inherits the earth and whoever is upon it, is that He causes all the creatures dwelling on the earth to die, and He, majestic and exalted is He, remains, because He is the Living who does not die. Then they will be returned to Him on the Day of Resurrection. He has indicated this meaning in other places, such as His saying: ﴿Everyone upon it will perish, and there will remain the Face of your Lord, Owner of Majesty and Honor﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 26-27], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors﴾ [Al-Hijr: 23], and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 41:

God Almighty's words: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which hears not and sees not and avails you nothing?"﴾ ﴿"O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.﴾ ﴿"O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has been to the Most Merciful a disobedient one."﴾ ﴿"O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan."﴾ In this noble verse, God Almighty commanded His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to mention in the Book, which is the Great Qur'an sent down to him from God, Abraham (peace be upon him and upon our Prophet), and to recite to the people in the Qur'an his story with his people and his call to them to worship God alone and to abandon the worship of idols, which neither hear, nor see, nor benefit, nor harm. God repeated this meaning mentioned in these verses in other verses of His Book, Almighty is He. So what He commanded His Prophet here, to mention in the Book Abraham: ﴿When he said to his father, "O my father, why do you worship that which hears not and sees not"﴾ [Maryam: 42] and so on, He explained it in surah "al-Shu'ara'" in His words: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham.﴾ ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What do you worship?"﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 69-70].

So His words here, ﴿And mention in the Book﴾, have the meaning of His words: ﴿And recite to them the news of Abraham.﴾ In "al-Shu'ara'" He added that what he said to his father about forbidding the worship of idols, he said also to all his people. God repeated the report about this prohibition, which he addressed to his father and his people concerning the worship of idols, in other places, such as:

• His words: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error."﴾ [al-An'am: 74].

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are you worshipping?" They said, "We worship idols and remain devoted to them." He said, "Do they hear you when you call? Or do they benefit you or harm?" They said, "Rather, we found our fathers doing thus." He said, "Have you considered what you have been worshipping, you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of the worlds."﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 70-77].

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were well-acquainted with him. When he said to his father and his people, "What are these statues to which you are devoted?" They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them." He said, "You and your fathers have certainly been in manifest error." They said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jokers?" He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am of those who testify to that."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 51-56].

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father and his people, "Indeed, I am free of that which you worship, except He who created me, for indeed He will guide me."﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 26-27].

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, among his followers was Abraham, when he came to his Lord with a sound heart, when he said to his father and his people, "What is it that you worship? Is it a falsehood, gods other than God, that you desire? So what is your opinion of the Lord of the worlds?"﴾ [al-Saffat: 83-87].

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, "Indeed, we are free of you and whatever you worship other than God. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone," except for the statement of Abraham to his father, "I will surely ask forgiveness for you."﴾ [al-Mumtahanah: 4].

And other verses besides these.

His words in this verse: ﴿When he said to his father﴾, the adverb which is ﴿idh﴾ is a badal al-ishtimal (substitution of inclusion, i.e. a noun that includes what precedes it) of ﴿Abraham﴾ in His words: ﴿And mention in the Book Abraham﴾, as its counterpart was mentioned earlier in His words: ﴿And mention in the Book Maryam, when she withdrew﴾ [Maryam: 16]. We have already mentioned there the denial of some scholars of this i'rab (grammatical analysis). The clause ﴿Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet﴾ [Maryam: 41] is parenthetical between the substitute and the substituted noun, according to the i'rab mentioned. The word ﴿siddiq﴾ is an intensive form (sigha mubalaghah) from truthfulness, due to the great truthfulness of Abraham in his dealings with his Lord and the truthfulness of his speech, as God bore witness to his truthful dealing in His words: ﴿And Abraham who fulfilled [his trust]﴾ [al-Najm: 37], and His words: ﴿And when Abraham was tried by his Lord with commands, and he fulfilled them, He said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people."﴾ [al-Baqarah: 124].

From his truthfulness in dealing with his Lord: his consent to slaughter his son, and his proceeding in fact to do so in obedience to his Lord, although the child is a piece of the liver.(p-425)

Yet our children are between us, our livers walking upon the earth.

God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead, We called to him, "O Abraham! You have fulfilled the vision."﴾ [al-Saffat: 103-105].

And from his truthfulness in dealing with his Lord: his patience upon being thrown into the fire, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are to act."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 68], and He said: ﴿So the answer of his people was only that they said, "Kill him or burn him," but God saved him from the fire.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 24].

The scholars of tafsir (exegesis) mentioned in his story that when they threw him into the fire, Gabriel met him and asked him, "Do you have a need?" He said, "As for to you, no; as for to God, yes." Gabriel said to him, "Why do you not ask Him?" He said, "His knowledge of my condition is sufficient instead of my asking."

And from his truthfulness in dealing with his Lord: his patience upon leaving family and homeland in flight with his religion, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿So Lot believed him, and he said, "Indeed, I am emigrating to my Lord."﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 26]. He emigrated from the land of Iraq to Damascus. God, Exalted is He, has made clear in other places that he did not suffice with forbidding them from the worship of idols and explaining that they neither benefit nor harm, but went further, for he broke them into pieces, making them fragments, and left the largest of the idols. When they asked him whether he was the one who broke them, he said to them, "Rather, the largest of them did it, so ask them if they can speak." God, Exalted is He, said about him: ﴿And by God, I will surely plan against your idols after you have turned away, retreating.﴾ ﴿So he reduced them to fragments, except a large one among them, that they might return to it.﴾ ﴿They said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿They said, "We heard a young man mention them; he is called Abraham."﴾ ﴿They said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people that they may testify."﴾ ﴿They said, "Are you the one who did this to our gods, O Abraham?"﴾ ﴿He said, "Rather, this, the largest of them, did it; so ask them, if they can speak."﴾ ﴿So they returned to themselves and said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ ﴿Then they were turned back upon their heads, [and said], "You know these do not speak."﴾ ﴿He said, "Do you then worship other than God that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ ﴿"Uff to you and to what you worship other than God! Do you not then use reason?"﴾ [al-Anbiya': 57-67]. And He said: ﴿So he turned to their gods and said, "Will you not eat?"﴾ ﴿"What is [wrong] with you that you do not speak?"﴾ ﴿Then he turned upon them, striking with the right hand.﴾ ﴿Then they came to him hastening.﴾ ﴿He said, "Do you worship that which you carve?"﴾ ﴿"And God created you and what you do."﴾ [al-Saffat: 91-96]. His words: ﴿Then he turned upon them, striking with the right hand﴾ mean: he inclined toward the idols, striking them with his right hand until he made them fragments, i.e., broken pieces, from their saying: "jadhdhahu," when he cut it and broke it.

His words, Exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, he was a man of truth﴾ mean: one who is very truthful. It is known from him that the three lies mentioned in the hadith about Abraham were all for the sake of God, Exalted is He, and that in reality they belong to truthfulness and not to lying in its literal sense. Further clarification of this will come, God willing, in surah "al-Anbiya'".(p-426)

His words, Exalted is He, about Abraham: ﴿Yā abati﴾ (O my father). The ta' in it is a substitute (iwad) for the ya' of the speaker (the possessive "my"). The original is "yā abī", as he indicated in the Khulasah (Ibn Malik's Alfiyyah) with his words:

In the vocative, "abat" and "ummat," make it open or with a kasra, and the ta' is a substitute for the ya' [of the speaker].

His words, Exalted is He, in this verse: ﴿Lima ta'budu﴾ (why do you worship): its original is "ma," the interrogative, so the preposition which is "al-lam" entered upon it, and its alif was deleted according to his words in the Khulasah:

When "ma" is interrogative and a preposition enters upon it, its alif is deleted, and add a ha' when you pause.

It is known that recitation is a followed tradition (sunnah muttaba'ah) and is not permitted by analogy. Therefore one pauses on "lima" with a sukun on the mim, not with the ha' of pause, as in the verse. The meaning of his worship of Satan in His words: ﴿Do not worship Satan﴾ is his obedience to Satan in disbelief and sins. That is shirk of obedience, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Did I not charge you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾ ﴿And that you worship Me; this is a straight path.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 60-61]. This topic has been fully treated earlier in surah "al-Isra'" and elsewhere.

The verse indicates that the disbelievers who are punished on the Day of Resurrection are the allies of Satan, due to His words here: ﴿Indeed, I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will touch you, so you would be a companion to Satan﴾ [Maryam: 45]. The verses that indicate that the disbelievers are the allies of Satan are numerous, and we have mentioned much of that earlier in surah "al-Kahf" and elsewhere, such as:

• His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So fight against the allies of Satan﴾ [al-Nisa': 76].

• His words: ﴿That is only Satan instilling fear of his allies﴾ [Al 'Imran: 175], meaning: he frightens you with his allies.

• His words: ﴿Indeed, they took the devils as allies instead of God﴾ [al-A'raf: 30], and other verses as previously mentioned. Whoever Satan adorns disbelief and sins for, and who follows him in that in this world, has no ally in the Hereafter except Satan, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿By God, We had already sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made attractive to them their deeds, so he is their ally today, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ [al-Nahl: 63].

Whoever has no ally on the Day of Resurrection except Satan, it is established that he has no ally who will benefit him on the Day of Resurrection.

His words, Exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you﴾ [Maryam: 43] (p-427) mean: what God taught him of revelation and what He inspired him with while he was young, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had certainly given Abraham his sound judgment before, and We were well-acquainted with him.﴾ [al-Anbiya': 51]. Abraham's argument with his people, as we mentioned some of the verses indicating it, is praised by God through them, and He made clear that it is the argument of God which He gave to His Prophet Abraham, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people; We raise by degrees whom We will.﴾ [al-An'am: 83], and God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And his people argued with him. He said, "Do you argue with me concerning God while He has guided me?"﴾ [al-An'am: 80]. That the verses mentioned are related to his argument with them mentioned in surah "al-An'am" does not contradict what we have mentioned, because the origin of the argument is in one matter, which is the Oneness of God, Exalted is He, and establishing the decisive proof that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him alone, Exalted is He, in surah "al-An'am" and in other surahs. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 46:

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿قالَ أراغِبٌ أنْتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي ياإبْراهِيمُ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ لَأرْجُمَنَّكَ واهْجُرْنِي مَلِيًّا﴾ ﴿قالَ سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ سَأسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي إنَّهُ كانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "Do you turn away from my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you, so leave me alone for a long time." He said, "Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you. Indeed, He has always been gracious to me."﴾

بَيِّنَ اللَّهُ جَلَّ وعَلا في هاتَيْنِ الآيَتَيْنِ الكَرِيمَتَيْنِ: أنَّ إبْراهِيمَ لِمّا نَصَحَ أباهُ النَّصِيحَةَ المَذْكُورَةَ مَعَ ما فِيها مِنَ الرِّفْقِ واللِّينِ، وإيضاحِ الحَقِّ والتَّحْذِيرِ مِن عِبادَةِ ما لا يَسْمَعُ ولا يُبْصِرُ، ومِن عَذابِ اللَّهِ تَعالى ووِلايَةِ الشَّيْطانِ - خاطَبَهُ هَذا الخِطابَ العَنِيفَ، وسَمّاهُ بِاسْمِهِ ولَمْ يَقُلْ لَهُ ”يا بُنَيَّ“ في مُقابَلَةِ قَوْلِهِ لَهُ ”يا أبَتِ“ وأنْكَرَ عَلَيْهِ أنَّهُ راغِبٌ عَنْ عِبادَةِ الأوْثانِ، أيْ: مُعْرِضٌ عَنْها لا يُرِيدُها؛ لِأنَّهُ لا يَعْبُدُ إلّا ال لَّهَ وحْدَهُ جَلَّ وعَلا، وهَدَّدَهُ بِأنَّهُ إنْ لَمْ يَنْتَهِ عَمّا يَقُولُهُ لَهُ لَيَرْجُمَنَّهُ ) قِيَلَ بِالحِجارَةِ وقِيلَ بِاللِّسانِ شَتْمًا ( والأوَّلُ أظْهَرُ، ثُمَّ أمَرَهُ بِهَجْرِهِ مَلِيًّا أيْ: زَمانًا طَوِيلًا، ثُمَّ بَيَّنَ أنَّ إبْراهِيمَ قابَلَ أيْضًا جَوابَهُ العَنِيفَ بِغايَةِ الرِّفْقِ واللِّينِ في قَوْلِهِ: قالَ ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ سَأسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي﴾ الآيَةَ [مريم: ٤٧]، وخِطابُ إبْراهِيمَ لِأبِيهِ الجاهِلِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ﴾ قَدْ بَيَّنَ جَلَّ وعَلا أنَّهُ خِطابُ عِبادِهِ المُؤْمِنِينَ لِلْجُهّالِ إذا خاطَبُوهم، كَما قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلى الأرْضِ هَوْنًا وإذا خاطَبَهُمُ الجاهِلُونَ قالُوا سَلامًا﴾ [الفرقان: ٦٣]، وقالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَإذا سَمِعُوا اللَّغْوَ أعْرَضُوا عَنْهُ وقالُوا لَنا أعْمالُنا ولَكم أعْمالُكم سَلامٌ عَلَيْكم لا نَبْتَغِي الجاهِلِينَ﴾ [القصص: ٥٥]، وما ذَكَرَهُ تَعالى هُنا مِن أنَّ إبْراهِيمَ لَمّا أقْنَعَ أباهُ بِالحُجَّةِ القاطِعَةِ، قابَلَهُ أبُوهُ بِالعُنْفِ والشِّدَّةِ بَيَّنَ في مَواضِعَ أُخَرَ أنَّهُ هو عادَةُ الكُفّارِ المُتَعَصِّبِينَ لِأصْنامِهِمْ، كُلَّما أُفْحِمُوا بِالحُجَّةِ القاطِعَةِ لَجَئُوا إلى اسْتِعْمالِ القُوَّةِ، كَقَوْلِهِ تَعالى عَنْ إبْراهِيمَ لَمّا قالَ لَهُ الكُفّارُ عَنْ أصْنامِهِمْ: (p-٤٢٨)﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ ما هَؤُلاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ٦٥]، قالَ: ﴿أُفٍّ لَكم ولِما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ أفَلا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ٦٧]، فَلَمّا أفْحَمَهم بِهَذِهِ الحُجَّةِ لَجَئُوا إلى القُوَّةِ، كَما قالَ تَعالى عَنْهم: ﴿قالُوا حَرِّقُوهُ وانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكم إنْ كُنْتُمْ فاعِلِينَ﴾ [الأنبياء: ٦٨]، ونَظِيرُهُ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى عَنْ قَوْمِ إبْراهِيمَ: ﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلّا أنْ قالُوا اقْتُلُوهُ أوْ حَرِّقُوهُ فَأنْجاهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ النّارِ﴾ الآيَةَ [العنكبوت: ٢٤]، وقَوْلُهُ عَنْ قَوْمِ لُوطٍ لَمّا أفْحَمَهم بِالحُجَّةِ: ﴿فَما كانَ جَوابَ قَوْمِهِ إلّا أنْ قالُوا أخْرِجُوا آلَ لُوطٍ مِن قَرْيَتِكُمْ﴾ الآيَةَ [النمل: ٥٦]، إلى غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنَ الآياتِ.

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿سَلامٌ عَلَيْكَ﴾، يَعْنِي: لا يَنالُكَ مِنِّي أذًى ولا مَكْرُوهٌ، بَلْ سَتَسْلَمُ مِنِّي فَلا أُوذِيكَ، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿سَأسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي﴾، وعْدٌ مِن إبْراهِيمَ لِأبِيهِ بِاسْتِغْفارِهِ لَهُ، وقَدْ وفّى بِذَلِكَ الوَعْدِ، كَما قالَ تَعالى عَنْهُ: ﴿واغْفِرْ لِأبِي إنَّهُ كانَ مِنَ الضّالِّينَ﴾ [مريم: ٤٧]، وكَما قالَ تَعالى عَنْهُ: ﴿رَبَّنا اغْفِرْ لِي ولِوالِدَيَّ ولِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الحِسابُ﴾ [إبراهيم: ٤١] .

وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ لَمّا بَيَّنَ لَهُ أنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأ مِنهُ، ولَمْ يَسْتَغْفِرْ لَهُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ، كَما قالَ تَعالى: ﴿فَلَمّا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ أنَّهُ عَدُوٌّ لِلَّهِ تَبَرَّأ مِنهُ إنَّ إبْراهِيمَ لَأوّاهٌ حَلِيمٌ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٤]، وقَدْ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إبْراهِيمَ لِأبِيهِ إلّا عَنْ مَوْعِدَةٍ وعَدَها إيّاهُ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٤]، والمَوْعِدَةُ المَذْكُورَةُ هي قَوْلُهُ هُنا: ﴿سَأسْتَغْفِرُ لَكَ رَبِّي﴾ الآيَةَ [مريم: ٤٧]، ولَمّا اقْتَدى المُؤْمِنُونَ بِإبْراهِيمَ فاسْتَغْفَرُوا لِمَوْتاهُمُ المُشْرِكِينَ، واسْتَغْفَرَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ لِعَمِّهِ أبِي طالِبٍ أنْزَلَ اللَّهُ فِيهِمْ: ﴿ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ ولَوْ كانُوا أُولِي قُرْبى مِن بَعْدِ ما تَبَيَّنَ لَهم أنَّهم أصْحابُ الجَحِيمِ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٣]، ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿وَما كانَ اسْتِغْفارُ إبْراهِيمَ لِأبِيهِ﴾ الآيَةَ [التوبة: ١١٤]، وبَيَّنَ في سُورَةِ ”المُمْتَحِنَةِ“ أنَّ الِاسْتِغْفارَ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ مُسْتَثْنًى مِنَ الأُسْوَةِ بِإبْراهِيمَ، والأُسْوَةُ الِاقْتِداءُ، وذَلِكَ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿قَدْ كانَتْ لَكم أُسْوَةٌ حَسَنَةٌ في إبْراهِيمَ والَّذِينَ مَعَهُ إذْ قالُوا لِقَوْمِهِمْ إنّا بُرَآءُ مِنكم ومِمّا تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ - إلى قَوْلِهِ - ﴿إلّا قَوْلَ إبْراهِيمَ لِأبِيهِ لَأسْتَغْفِرَنَّ لَكَ﴾ [الممتحنة: ٤]، أيْ: فَلا أُسْوَةَ لَكم في إبْراهِيمَ في ذَلِكَ، ولَمّا نَدِمَ المُسْلِمُونَ عَلى اسْتِغْفارِهِمْ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ حِينَ قالَ فِيهِمْ: ﴿ما كانَ لِلنَّبِيِّ والَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أنْ يَسْتَغْفِرُوا لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ الآيَةَ [التوبة: ١١٣]، بَيَّنَ اللَّهُ تَعالى أنَّهم مَعْذُورُونَ في ذَلِكَ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يُبَيِّنْ لَهم مَنعَ ذَلِكَ قَبْلَ فِعْلِهِ، وذَلِكَ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿وَما كانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْمًا بَعْدَ إذْ هَداهم حَتّى يُبَيِّنَ لَهم ما يَتَّقُونَ﴾ [التوبة: ١١٥] .

وَقَوْلُهُ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ: ﴿أراغِبٌ أنْتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي﴾، يَجُوزُ فِيهِ أنْ يَكُونَ ”راغِبٌ“ خَبَرًا (p-٤٢٩)مُقَدَّمًا، و ”أنْتَ“ مُبْتَدَأً مُؤَخَّرًا، وأنْ يَكُونَ ”أراغِبٌ“ مُبْتَدَأً، و ”أنْتَ“ فاعِلٌ سَدَّ مَسَدَّ الخَبَرِ، ويَتَرَجَّحُ هَذا الإعْرابُ الأخِيرُ عَلى الأوَّلِ مِن وجْهَيْنِ: الأوَّلُ أنَّهُ لا يَكُونُ فِيهِ تَقْدِيمٌ ولا تَأْخِيرٌ، والأصْلُ في الخَبَرِ التَّأْخِيرُ كَما هو مَعْلُومٌ، الوَجْهُ الثّانِي هو ألّا يَكُونَ فُصِلَ بَيْنَ العامِلِ الَّذِي هو ”أراغِبٌ“، وبَيْنَ مَعْمُولِهِ الَّذِي هو ”عَنْ آلِهَتِي“ بِما لَيْسَ بِمَعْمُولٍ لِلْعامِلِ؛ لِأنَّ الخَبَرَ لَيْسَ هو عامِلًا في المُبْتَدَأِ، بِخِلافِ كَوْنِ ”أنْتَ“ فاعِلًا، فَإنَّهُ مَعْمُولُ ”أراغِبٌ“ فَلَمْ يُفْصَلْ بَيْنَ ”أراغِبٌ“ وبَيْنَ ”عَنْ آلِهَتِي“ بِأجْنَبِيٍّ، وإنَّما فُصِلَ بَيْنَهُما بِمَعْمُولِ المُبْتَدَأِ الَّذِي هو فاعِلُهُ السّادُّ مَسَدَّ خَبَرِهِ، والرَّغْبَةُ عَنِ الشَّيْءِ: تَرْكُهُ عَمْدًا لِلزُّهْدِ فِيهِ وعَدَمِ الحاجَةِ إلَيْهِ، وقَدْ قَدَّمْنا في سُورَةِ ”النِّساءِ“ الفَرْقَ بَيْنَ قَوْلِهِمْ: رَغِبَ عَنْهُ، وقَوْلِهِمْ: رَغِبَ فِيهِ. في الكَلامِ عَلى قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَتَرْغَبُونَ أنْ تَنْكِحُوهُنَّ﴾ الآيَةَ [النساء: ١٢٧]، والتَّحْقِيقُ في قَوْلِهِ ”مَلِيًّا“ أنَّ المُرادَ بِهِ الزَّمَنُ الطَّوِيلُ ومِنهُ قَوْلُ مُهَلْهَلٍ:

؎فَتَصَدَّعَتْ صُمُّ الجِبالِ لِمَوْتِهِ وبَكَتْ عَلَيْهِ المُرَمَّلاتُ مَلِيًّا

وَأصْلُهُ واوِيُّ اللّامِ؛ لِأنَّهُ مِنَ المِلاوَةِ وهي مُدَّةُ العَيْشِ، ومِن ذَلِكَ قِيلَ اللَّيْلُ والنَّهارُ المَلَوانِ، ومِنهُ قَوْلُ ابْنِ مُقْبِلٍ:

؎ألا يا دِيارَ الحَيِّ بِالسَّبُعانِ ∗∗∗ أمَلَّ عَلَيْها بِالبِلى المَلَوانِ

وَقَوْلُ الآخَرِ:

؎نَهارٌ ولَيْلٌ دائِمٌ مَلَواهُما ∗∗∗ عَلى كُلِّ حالِ المَرْءِ يَخْتَلِفانِ

وَقِيلَ: المَلَوانِ في بَيْتِ ابْنِ مُقْبِلٍ: طَرَفا النَّهارِ.

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿إنَّهُ كانَ بِي حَفِيًّا﴾، أيْ: لَطِيفًا بِي، كَثِيرَ الإحْسانِ إلَيَّ، وجُمْلَةُ: ﴿واهْجُرْنِي﴾ عَطْفٌ عَلى جُمْلَةِ ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ لَأرْجُمَنَّكَ﴾، وذَلِكَ دَلِيلٌ عَلى جَوازِ عَطْفِ الجُمْلَةِ الإنْشائِيَّةِ عَلى الجُمْلَةِ الخَبَرِيَّةِ، ونَظِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِن كَلامِ العَرَبِ قَوْلُ امْرِئِ القَيْسِ:

؎وَإنَّ شِفائِي عَبْرَةٌ إنْ سَفَحْتُها ∗∗∗ فَهَلْ عِنْدَ رَسْمٍ دارِسٍ مِن مُعَوَّلِ

فَجُمْلَةُ ”وَإنَّ شِفائِي“ خَبَرِيَّةٌ، وجُمْلَةُ ”وَهَلْ عِنْدَ رَسْمٍ“ . . . إلَخْ إنْشائِيَّةٌ مَعْطُوفَةٌ عَلَيْها.

وَقَوْلُ الآخَرِ أيْضًا:

؎تُناغِي غَزالًا عِنْدَ بابِ ابْنِ عامِرٍ ∗∗∗ وكَحِّلْ مَآقِيَكَ الحِسانَ بِإثْمِدِ

وَهَذا هو الظّاهِرُ كَما قالَهُ أبُو حَيّانَ عَنْ سِيبَوَيْهَ، وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ في الكَشّافِ: فَإنْ (p-٤٣٠)قُلْتَ: عَلامَ عَطَفَ واهْجُرْنِي ؟ قُلْتُ عَلى مَعْطُوفٍ عَلَيْهِ مَحْذُوفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ ”لَأرْجُمَنَّكَ“ أيْ: فاحْذَرْنِي واهْجُرْنِي؛ لِأنَّ لَأرْجُمَنَّكَ تَهْدِيدٌ وتَقْرِيعٌ. اهـ.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 51:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And mention in the Book Moses; indeed he was chosen (mukhlaṣan), and he was a messenger and a prophet﴾. Know that in His saying "mukhlaṣan" there are two canonical readings (qira'atan sab'iyyatan). ʿĀṣim, Ḥamzah and al-Kisā'ī read it with a fatḥah on the lām, in the form of the passive participle (ism al-maf'ūl), and the meaning according to this reading is that God selected him and chose him. This meaning is supported by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "O Moses, I have chosen you above the people by My messages and by My speech"﴾ [al-A'raf: 144], and among what resembles this reading in the Qur'an is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We made them sincere (akhlaṣnāhum) with a pure quality, the remembrance of the Abode﴾ [Sad: 46]. Those whom God made sincere are thus "al-mukhlaṣūn" with a fatḥah on the lām. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it "mukhliṣan" with a kasrah on the lām, in the form of the active participle (ism al-fā'il), like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they were not commanded except to worship God, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-Bayyinah: 5], and His saying, may He be exalted:

﴿Say, "It is God I worship, sincere to Him in my religion"﴾ [al-Zumar: 14]. The verse.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿وَنادَيْناهُ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ الأيْمَنِ وقَرَّبْناهُ نَجِيًّا﴾. قالَ ابْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ في تَفْسِيرِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ الكَرِيمَةِ: يَقُولُ تَعالى ذِكْرُهُ: ونادَيْنا مُوسى مِن ناحِيَةِ الجَبَلِ، ويَعْنِي بِالأيْمَنِ يَمِينَ مُوسى؛ لِأنَّ الجَبَلَ لا يَمِينَ لَهُ ولا شِمالَ، وإنَّما ذَلِكَ كَما يُقالُ: قامَ عَنْ يَمِينِ القِبْلَةِ وعَنْ شِمالِها. وهَذِهِ القِصَّةُ جاءَتْ مُبَيَّنَةً في مَواضِعَ مُتَعَدِّدَةٍ مِن كِتابِ اللَّهِ تَعالى، وذَلِكَ أنَّ مُوسى لَمّا قَضى الأجَلَ الَّذِي بَيْنَهُ وبَيْنَ صِهْرِهِ، وسارَ بِأهْلِهِ راجِعًا مِن مَدْيَنَ إلى مِصْرَ، آنَسَ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ نارًا، فَذَهَبَ إلى تِلْكَ النّارِ لِيَجِدَ عِنْدَها مَن يَدُلُّهُ عَلى الطَّرِيقِ، ولِيَأْتِيَ بِجَذْوَةٍ مِنها لِيُوقِدَ بِها النّارَ لِأهْلِهِ لِيَصْطَلُوا بِها، فَناداهُ اللَّهُ وأرْسَلَهُ إلى فِرْعَوْنَ، وشَفَّعَهُ في أخِيهِ هارُونَ فَأرْسَلَهُ مَعَهُ، وأراهُ في ذَلِكَ الوَقْتِ مُعْجِزَةَ العَصا واليَدِ لِيَسْتَأْنِسَ بِذَلِكَ قَبْلَ حُضُورِهِ عِنْدَ فِرْعَوْنَ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمّا رَأى العَصا في المَرَّةِ الأُولى صارَتْ ثُعْبانًا ولّى مُدْبِرًا ولَمْ يُعَقِّبْ، فَلَوْ فَعَلَ ذَلِكَ عِنْدَما انْقَلَبَتْ ثُعْبانًا لَمّا طالَبَهُ فِرْعَوْنُ وقَوْمُهُ بِآيَةٍ، لَكانَ ذَلِكَ غَيْرَ لائِقٍ، ولِأجْلِ هَذا مُرِّنَ عَلَيْها في أوَّلِ مَرَّةٍ لِيَكُونَ مُسْتَأْنِسًا غَيْرَ خائِفٍ مِنها حِينَ تَصِيرُ ثُعْبانًا مُبِينًا. قالَ تَعالى في سُورَةِ ”طه“: ﴿وَهَلْ أتاكَ حَدِيثُ مُوسى﴾ ﴿إذْ رَأى نارًا فَقالَ لِأهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إنِّي آنَسْتُ نارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكم مِنها بِقَبَسٍ أوْ أجِدُ عَلى النّارِ هُدًى﴾ ﴿فَلَمّا أتاها نُودِيَ يامُوسى﴾ ﴿إنِّي أنا رَبُّكَ فاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ إنَّكَ بِالوادِي المُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ ﴿وَأنا اخْتَرْتُكَ فاسْتَمِعْ لِما يُوحى﴾ ﴿إنَّنِي أنا اللَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلّا أنا فاعْبُدْنِي وأقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾ [طه: ٨ - ١٣]. (p-٤٣١) وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَنادَيْناهُ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ الأيْمَنِ﴾ [مريم: ٥٢]، هو مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ في ”طه“: ﴿فَلَمّا أتاها﴾ ﴿نُودِيَ يامُوسى﴾ ﴿إنِّي أنا رَبُّكَ﴾.

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿بِقَبَسٍ﴾، أيْ: شِهابٍ، بِدَلِيلِ قَوْلِهِ في ”النَّمْلِ“: ﴿أوْ آتِيكم بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكم تَصْطَلُونَ﴾ [طه: ٧]، وذَلِكَ هو المُرادُ بِالجَذْوَةِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِنَ النّارِ﴾ [القصص: ٢٩]، وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿أوْ أجِدُ عَلى النّارِ هُدًى﴾ [طه: ١٠]، أيْ: مَن يَهْدِينِي إلى الطَّرِيقِ ويَدُلُّنِي عَلَيْها، لِأنَّهم كانُوا ضَلُّوا الطَّرِيقَ، والزَّمَنُ زَمَنُ بَرْدٍ. وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿آنَسْتُ نارًا﴾ [طه: ١٠]، أيْ: أبْصَرْتُها. وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿فاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾ [طه: ١٢]، قالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: لِأنَّهُما كانَتا مِن جِلْدِ حِمارٍ غَيْرِ ذَكِيٍّ (أيْ غَيْرِ مُذَكًّى، أيْ غَيْرِ مَذْبُوحٍ ذَبْحًا شَرْعِيًّا)، ويُرْوى هَذا عَنْ كَعْبٍ وعِكْرِمَةَ وقَتادَةَ، نَقَلَهُ عَنْهُمُ القُرْطُبِيُّ وغَيْرُهُ، ورُوِيَ أيْضًا عَنْ عَلِيٍّ والحَسَنِ والزُّهْرِيِّ كَما رَواهُ عَنْهم صاحِبُ الدُّرِّ المَنثُورِ، ونَقَلَهُ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ وأبِي أيُّوبَ وغَيْرِ واحِدٍ مِنَ السَّلَفِ، ويُرْوى هَذا القَوْلُ عَنْ غَيْرِ مَن ذُكِرَ، وجاءَ فِيهِ حَدِيثٌ مَرْفُوعٌ مِن حَدِيثِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ رَواهُ التِّرْمِذِيُّ وغَيْرُهُ ولا يَصِحُّ، وفِيهِ أقْوالٌ أُخَرُ لِلْعُلَماءِ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ، وأظْهَرُها عِنْدِي، واللَّهُ تَعالى أعْلَمُ: أنَّ اللَّهَ أمَرَهُ بِخَلْعِ نَعْلَيْهِ، أيْ نَزْعِهِما مِن قَدَمَيْهِ، لِيُعَلِّمَهُ التَّواضُعَ لِرَبِّهِ حِينَ ناداهُ، فَإنَّ نِداءَ اللَّهِ لِعَبْدِهِ أمْرٌ عَظِيمٌ، يَسْتَوْجِبُ مِنَ العَبْدِ كَمالَ التَّواضُعِ والخُضُوعِ، واللَّهُ تَعالى أعْلَمُ.

وَقَوْلُ مَن قالَ: إنَّهُ أُمِرَ بِخَلْعِهِما احْتِرامًا لِلْبُقْعَةِ، يَدُلُّ لَهُ أنَّهُ أتْبَعَ أمْرَهُ بِخَلْعِهِما بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنَّكَ بِالوادِي المُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [طه: ١٢]، وقَدْ تَقَرَّرَ في ”مِسْكِ الإيماءِ والتَّنْبِيهِ“ أنَّ ”إنَّ“ مِن حُرُوفِ التَّعْلِيلِ (أيِ الحُرُوفِ الدَّالَّةِ عَلى العِلَّةِ)، وأظْهَرُ الأقْوالِ في قَوْلِهِ ”طُوًى“: أنَّهُ اسْمٌ لِلْوادِي، فَهو بَدَلٌ مِنَ الوادِي أوْ عَطْفُ بَيانٍ (أيْ تابِعٌ يُوَضِّحُ المَتْبُوعَ)، وفِيهِ أقْوالٌ أُخَرُ غَيْرُ ذَلِكَ.

وَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿وَأنا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾، أيْ: اصْطَفَيْتُكَ بِرِسالَتِي، كَقَوْلِهِ: ﴿إنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلى النّاسِ بِرِسالاتِي وبِكَلامِي﴾ [الأعراف: ١٤٤]. ومَعْنى الِاسْتِعْلاءِ في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿عَلى النّارِ﴾، أنَّ المُصْطَلِينَ بِالنّارِ يَسْتَعْلُونَ المَكانَ القَرِيبَ مِنها، ونَظِيرُ ذَلِكَ مِن كَلامِ العَرَبِ قَوْلُ الأعْشى:

تُشَبُّ لِمَقْرُورَيْنِ يَصْطَلِيانِها وباتَ عَلى النّارِ النَّدى والمُحَلَّقُ

قالَ تَعالى في سُورَةِ ”النَّمْلِ“: ﴿وَإنَّكَ لَتُلَقّى القُرْآنَ مِن لَدُنْ حَكِيمٍ عَلِيمٍ﴾ ﴿إذْ قالَ مُوسى لِأهْلِهِ إنِّي آنَسْتُ نارًا سَآتِيكم مِنها بِخَبَرٍ أوْ آتِيكم بِشِهابٍ قَبَسٍ لَعَلَّكم تَصْطَلُونَ﴾ ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَها نُودِيَ أنْ بُورِكَ مَن في النّارِ ومَن حَوْلَها وسُبْحانَ اللَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾ ﴿يامُوسى إنَّهُ أنا اللَّهُ العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ [النمل: ٦ - ٩]. فَقَوْلُهُ في ”النَّمْلِ“: ﴿فَلَمّا جاءَها نُودِيَ﴾ [النمل: ٨]، (p-٤٣٢) هُوَ مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ في ”مَرْيَمَ“: ﴿وَنادَيْناهُ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ الأيْمَنِ﴾ [مريم: ٥٢]، وقَوْلِهِ في ”طه“: ﴿فَلَمّا أتاها نُودِيَ يامُوسى﴾ [طه: ١١]. وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿سَآتِيكم مِنها بِخَبَرٍ﴾ [النمل: ٧]، هو مَعْنى قَوْلِهِ في ”طه“: ﴿أوْ أجِدُ عَلى النّارِ هُدًى﴾ [طه: ١٠]، أيْ: مَن يَدُلُّنِي عَلى الطَّرِيقِ فَيُخْبِرُنِي عَنْها، فَآتِيكم بِخَبَرِهِ عَنْها. وقالَ تَعالى في سُورَةِ ”القَصَصِ“: ﴿فَلَمّا قَضى مُوسى الأجَلَ وسارَ بِأهْلِهِ آنَسَ مِن جانِبِ الطُّورِ نارًا قالَ لِأهْلِهِ امْكُثُوا إنِّي آنَسْتُ نارًا لَعَلِّي آتِيكم مِنها بِخَبَرٍ أوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِنَ النّارِ لَعَلَّكم تَصْطَلُونَ﴾ ﴿فَلَمّا أتاها نُودِيَ مِن شاطِئِ الوادِي الأيْمَنِ في البُقْعَةِ المُبارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ﴾ الآيَةَ [القصص: ٢٩ - ٣٠].
