**The sixth issue**

Know that this great historical proof makes perfectly clear the natural stance of Muslims toward Western civilization. With this complete clarity, the beneficial is distinguished from the harmful, the good from the ugly, and the truth from falsehood. The complete, certain induction (*istiqra'*) shows that the aforementioned Western civilization includes both beneficial and harmful elements. As for its beneficial side, it is material, and its advancement in all material fields is too clear for me to explain. The benefits it contains for humanity are greater than what could be imagined; it has rendered enormous services to man insofar as he is an animal body. As for its harmful side, it is its complete neglect of the aspect that is the head of all good, and there is no good at all in this world without it: the spiritual upbringing of man and the refinement of his morals. This can only come through the light of heavenly revelation, which makes clear to man the path of happiness, draws for him wise plans in all fields of life, in this world and the next, and keeps him connected to his Lord at all times.

So Western civilization is rich in kinds of benefits from the first aspect, and utterly bankrupt from the second.

It is known that the domination of matter over spirit threatens the whole world with imminent danger and total destruction, as is now witnessed. Its problem can by no means be solved except by being illuminated by the light of heavenly revelation, which is the legislation of the Creator of the heavens and the earth; for whoever matter has made so arrogant that he rebels against his Creator and Provider will never prosper.

Correct division confines the attributes of the situation, which is the stance toward Western civilization, to four categories with no fifth, by rational confinement beyond doubt:

The first: abandoning this civilization, both its beneficial and its harmful parts.

The second: taking all of it, both harmful and beneficial.

The third: taking its harmful part and abandoning its beneficial part.

The fourth: taking its beneficial part and abandoning its harmful part.

Returning by correct elimination to these four categories, we find three of them false beyond doubt and one correct beyond doubt.

As for the three false ones: the first of them is abandoning all of it, and the invalidity of this is clear, because not engaging with material advancement leads to constant weakness, dependence and laziness, and contradicts the heavenly command in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you are able of power﴾ [al-Kahf: 60 — here cited as 8:60 in the source's numbering]. (Note: the source cites al-Kahf 60, which I have kept as given.)

A line of poetry:
The exalted nobility is not safe from harm, until blood is spilled on its sides.

The second of the false categories is taking all of it, because the moral degradation, the loss of spirituality and the lofty ideals of humanity that it contains are too clear for me to explain. It suffices to show this by its rebellion against the order of heaven and its disobedience to the Creator of this universe, may He be exalted: ﴿Has Allah permitted you, or do you invent against Allah?﴾ [Yunus: 59], ﴿Or do they have partners who have legislated for them of religion that for which Allah has not given permission?﴾ [al-Shura: 21]. The third of the false categories is taking the harmful and abandoning the beneficial, and there is no doubt that no one with the least discernment does this. Thus the correctness of the fourth category is established by correct division and elimination, which is taking the beneficial and abandoning the harmful.

And this is how he ﷺ acted. He benefited from digging the trench in the Battle of the Confederates, although that was a military plan of the Persians, which Salman informed him of, and he adopted it. The fact that its origin was among the unbelievers did not prevent him from it.

The Prophet ﷺ also intended to forbid intercourse with nursing women out of concern for their infants, because the Arabs believed that *al-ghila* (intercourse with a nursing woman) weakens and harms the child. Among this is the saying of the poet:

Horsemen who do not overdo nursing, so that the swords do not grow weak in their hands.

But the Persians and the Romans informed him ﷺ that they do this and it does not harm their children, so he took this medical practice from them, and the fact that its origin was among the unbelievers did not prevent him from it.

The Prophet ﷺ also benefited from the guidance of Ibn al-Uraiqit al-Du'ali on the road during the journey of the Hijra, although he was an unbeliever.

It becomes clear from this proof that the natural stance of Islam and Muslims toward Western civilization is to strive to acquire what it has produced in material respects, and to beware of what it has brought in rebellion against the Creator of the universe, may He be exalted, so that both this world and the next will be good for them. What is regrettable is that most of them reverse the matter: they take from it moral degradation, departure from religion, and distance from obedience to the Creator of the universe, and they gain no benefit from its material advantages. So they have lost this world and the next. That is the manifest loss.

How good are religion and the world when they are combined, and how ugly are disbelief and bankruptcy for a man. We have already presented a useful portion showing that religion does not contradict material advancement, in the discussion of surah al-Isra' on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most suitable﴾ [al-Isra': 9]; this suffices so that it need not be repeated here. It is known from the history of the Prophet ﷺ and his companions that they strove to advance in all fields while maintaining obedience to the Creator of the heavens and the earth, may He be exalted.

The most apparent of the opinions to me regarding the meaning of "covenant" in His saying, may He be exalted, in this noble verse: ﴿Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam: 78], is that the meaning is: "Or has Allah given him a covenant that He will do that for him," based on His saying, may He be exalted, in its parallel in surah al-Baqara: ﴿Say: Have you taken a covenant with Allah? Then Allah will not fail His covenant﴾ [al-Baqara: 80]. The best way to interpret the Qur'an is by the Qur'an. It has also been said that the covenant mentioned is good deeds, and it has been said that it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We shall record what he says, and We shall extend for him the punishment, an extension.﴾ ﴿And We shall inherit from him what he speaks of, and he will come to Us alone.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that He will record what that disbeliever said, fabricating against Him, namely that on the Day of Resurrection he will be given wealth and children despite his disbelief in Allah. And He says that He will extend for him the punishment, an extension. Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We shall extend for him the punishment, an extension﴾ [Maryam: 79], meaning: We will increase him in punishment upon punishment. Al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: ﴿And We shall extend for him the punishment﴾ means: We will lengthen for him from the punishment what befits him, and punish him with the kind of punishment with which the mockers are punished; or We will increase him in punishment and multiply for him the extension. It is said: madda-hu and amadda-hu have the same meaning, and the reading of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, "wa-numiddu lahu," with a damma, supports this.

He emphasised this with the verbal noun (maṣdar), and this is due to the intensity of Allah's anger; we seek refuge in Him from doing what would merit His anger. End of quotation.

The linguistic root of madad (extension) is increase. This meaning is supported by His saying, exalted is He, concerning the leaders of the disbelievers who disbelieved and barred from the way of Allah: ﴿We shall add to them punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption﴾ [al-Nahl: 88], and His saying concerning the followers and those they followed: ﴿He will say, "For each there is double, but you do not know"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38].

His saying in this verse: ﴿And We shall inherit from him what he speaks of﴾ [Maryam: 80], meaning: what he claims he will be given on the Day of Resurrection of wealth and children. That is, We will strip him in this world of the wealth and children We gave him, by destroying them. It was also said: We will deprive him of what he wished for of wealth and children in the Hereafter, and make it for the Muslims. The first meaning is supported by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned﴾ [Maryam: 40], and His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and We are the Inheritors﴾ [al-Hijr: 23], as its clarification has already preceded in this noble surah (p-508).

His saying: ﴿and he will come to Us alone﴾ means: solitary, having no wealth, no child, no servant, nor anything else, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And you have certainly come to Us alone, as We created you the first time﴾, the verse [al-An'am: 94], and He said, exalted is He: ﴿And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 95], as its clarification has already preceded.

If it is said: How did He, majestic and exalted, express in this noble verse with the particle of future deferral, which indicates the future, in His saying ﴿We shall record what he says﴾, even though what the disbeliever says is recorded without delay, as evidenced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer, ready﴾ [Qaf: 18]?

The answer: Al-Zamakhshari in his Kashshaf addressed the answer to this question with the following text:

I say: In it are two aspects. One of them: "We will make him know and inform him that We have recorded his saying," following the manner of the saying of Za'id ibn Sa'sa'a al-Faqa'si:

"When we are traced, you were not born of a base woman, and you did not find from acknowledging her any alternative."

Meaning: it became clear and known through lineage that I am not the son of a base woman.

The second: The one who threatens the offender says: "I will surely take revenge on you," meaning he does not fail to achieve victory even if time stretches out and is delayed; so he uses it here in the sense of threat. End of his words verbatim, except that we have added the name of the poem's speaker and its completion.

What He, majestic and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, that He records what this disbeliever says, He mentioned something similar in several places of His Book,

• such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Allah is swifter in plotting. Indeed, Our messengers record what you plot﴾ [Yunus: 21]

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private conversations? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 80],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿This is Our record; it speaks against you with truth. Indeed, We used to copy what you were doing﴾ [al-Jathiya: 29]

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 19]

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We shall record what they have said and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say, "Taste the punishment of the burning"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 181],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Recompense. But indeed, over you are guardians, noble and recording, who know what you do﴾ [al-Infitar: 9–11]

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this Book that leaves nothing small or great except that it has enumerated it?"﴾ [al-Kahf: 49],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find spread open. "Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner"﴾ [al-Isra': 13],

and other verses besides these.

(p-509) Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they have taken besides Allah gods, that they may be for them a source of might.﴾ ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposers to them.﴾

In this noble verse, Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentions that the disbelievers mentioned earlier in His words, ﴿And We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees﴾ [Maryam: 72], took besides Allah gods, meaning objects of worship, such as idols and others, which they worshipped besides Allah. They worshipped them so that they would be for them a source of might, that is, helpers and intercessors who would rescue them from the punishment of Allah. This is as Allah clarified their intention in His words: ﴿And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position."﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3]. Their bringing them nearer to Allah in position, in their assumption, is the might they hoped to gain through them. This is like His statement about them: ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ [Yunus: 18]. So intercession with Allah is, for them, a might that they claim through these beings, a lie and a fabrication against Allah, as He explained with His words: ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of that which He does not know in the heavens or on the earth? Exalted is He above what they associate."﴾ [Yunus: 18].

His words in this noble verse, "No!", are a rebuke and a deterrent against that corrupt, false assumption. That is, the matter is not as they think. The objects they worshipped besides Allah will not be a might for them; rather, the reverse will be true, and they will be opposers to them, that is, helpers against them in their disputes, in denying them, and in disowning them. The statements of the scholars concerning the verse revolve around what we have mentioned. Such as the statement of Ibn 'Abbas: "﴿Ḍidd﴾ means helpers." The statement of al-Ḍaḥḥak: "﴿Ḍidd﴾ means enemies." The statement of Qatadah: "﴿Ḍidd﴾ means companions in the Fire, cursing one another." And the statement of Ibn 'Aṭiyyah: "﴿Ḍidd﴾ means that there will come to them from them the opposite of what they hoped for, so that will lead them to humiliation and disgrace, the opposite of the might they hoped for."

This meaning which Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, mentioned in this noble verse, He also clarified in other places, such as His words: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their supplication, are unaware. And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5–6]. And His words: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those you call upon besides Him do not possess [even] a thin membrane of a date seed. If you call upon them, they do not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association. And none can inform you like one [who is] Acquainted.﴾ [Fatir: 13–14], and other verses.

As for the pronoun of the subject in His words, ﴿they will deny﴾ (sayakfurūna), there are two views among the scholars, and each of them is supported by the Qur'an, but one of them has an indicator that favors it over the other.

(p-510) The first view: the wāw of the subject in His words ﴿they will deny﴾ refers to the objects of worship that they used to worship besides Allah. As for those among them who are rational, there is no problem with this. As for those that are not rational, Allah is capable of creating for them a perception by which they address those who worshipped them, and by which they deny their worship of them. This view is supported by His words about them: ﴿We disassociate ourselves before You; it was not us they were worshipping.﴾ [Al-Qasas: 63]. And His words: ﴿And when those who associated [others with Allah] see their associates, they will say, "Our Lord, these are our associates whom we used to call upon besides You." But they will throw at them the statement, "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ [An-Nahl: 86]. And His words: ﴿And their associates will say, "You did not used to worship us." So sufficient is Allah as a witness between us and you; indeed, we were unaware of your worship.﴾ [Yunus: 28–29], and other verses.

The second view: the worshippers are the ones who deny their worship of their associates and disown it. This view is supported by His words: ﴿Then their [only] trial will be that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not those who associated."﴾ [Al-An'am: 23], and His statement about them: ﴿Rather, we did not used to call upon anything before﴾ [Ghafir: 74], and other verses.

The indicator that favors the first view is that the pronoun in His words ﴿and they will be﴾ refers to the objects of worship. Accordingly, the reference of the pronoun in ﴿they will deny﴾ to the objects of worship is more apparent, because the pronouns are consistent with one another.

As for the second view, the pronoun in ﴿they will deny﴾ would refer to the worshippers, while the pronoun in ﴿they will be﴾ would refer to those worshipped. Separating the pronouns contradicts what is apparent. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

As for the statement of some scholars that "no" in this verse is connected to what follows it and not to what precedes it, and that the meaning is: "No! They will deny," that is, "Truly they will deny their worship," this is possible. But the first view is more apparent and more preponderant than it, and its proponent is more numerous. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted. Regarding His word "no" (kallā), there are irregular (shādhdh) readings, and we have left discussing them because of their irregularity.

As for His statement in this verse, ﴿that they may be for them a source of might (ʿizzan)﴾, He used the singular "ʿizz" although the intended meaning is plural, because its original form is a verbal noun (maṣdar), following the rule stated in the Alfiyyah (Ibn Mālik's poem on grammar):

"They described [nouns] with a frequent verbal noun, so they were bound to use the singular and the masculine form."

Describing with a verbal noun follows the rule of describing with an adjective. His word "ḍiddan" in the singular was also meant as plural. Ibn 'Aṭiyyah said: "Because it is originally a verbal noun." Abu Ḥayyan related this from him in al-Baḥr. (p-511) Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Ḍidd means helper. It is used in the singular in the same way as His statement, peace be upon him: 'They are one hand against whoever is other than them,' because of the unity of their word and because they are like one thing due to their intense solidarity and agreement."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 84:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not be hasty against them; We are but counting for them a counted number﴾.

His saying: ﴿So do not be hasty against them﴾ [Maryam: 84], i.e., do not seek to hasten the descent of punishment upon them, for Allah has set for it a specific, counted term. When that term ends, the punishment will come upon them. His saying: ﴿We are but counting for them a counted number﴾, i.e., We count the years, months and days that remain before the time of their destruction. When the appointed time for that arrives, We will destroy them. The Arabs say: "I hastened against him with such-and-such" (ʿajiltu ʿalayhi bi-kadhā) when you urge him to hasten it from him.

Among what He, may He be majestic and exalted, mentioned in this noble verse is that the destruction of the disbelievers has been assigned a counted term. He mentioned this in many places in His Book, such as:

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not hasten on their behalf. As if, on the day they see what they are promised, they had not remained but an hour of a day﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and had there not been a specified term, the punishment would have come to them﴾ [al-ʿAnkabut: 53], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿And We do not delay it except for a counted term﴾ [Hud: 104].

• His saying: ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a counted nation, they will surely say: what holds it back?﴾ [Hud: 8].

• His saying: ﴿And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42].

• His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little, then We will force them to a severe punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24].

• His saying: ﴿He said: as for one who disbelieves, I will grant him enjoyment for a little, then I will force him to the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126], to the end of the verse.

• His saying: ﴿So give respite to the disbelievers; give them respite gradually﴾ [al-Tariq: 17].

And other verses besides these.

It is narrated that al-Ma'mun recited this noble surah and came to this verse while a group of jurists was with him. He gestured to Ibn al-Sammak to admonish him, so he said: "If breaths are by number, and there is no extension for them, how quickly they will be exhausted."

The more apparent meaning of the verse is what we have mentioned: that the counting referred to is the counting of years, days and months of the appointed term.

Some scholars said: it is the counting of their breaths, as Ibn al-Sammak alluded to in his admonition to al-Ma'mun that we mentioned, if that is authentic. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that "when he recited it, he would weep and say: The last of the count is the departure of your soul; the last of the count is the separation from your family; the last of the count is the entry into your grave."

Some scholars said: ﴿We are but counting for them a counted number﴾ means: We count their deeds in order to recompense them for them. The apparent meaning is what we have already presented, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 85:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation,﴾ ﴿and drive the criminals to Hell like thirsty cattle.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the God-fearing, who used to fear Him in the abode of this world by complying with His command and avoiding His prohibition, will be gathered to Him on the Day of Resurrection in the state of being a delegation (wafd). According to verification, wafd is the plural of wafid, like sahib and sahb, and rakib and rakb. We have mentioned in Surat an-Nahl (the chapter of the Bee) that the verified view is that the form fa'l (with a fatha followed by a sukun) is among the plural patterns of abundance (jumu' al-kathrah) used for the active participle as a descriptive noun, and we have shown evidence for this from the Arabic language, even though the morphologists (al-Sarfiyyun) have overlooked it. The wafid is one who comes to a king, for example, concerning a matter of importance. Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning of His saying, ﴿wafdan﴾ [Maryam: 85], is riders (rukban). Some scholars say they will be riders on swift she-camels (najaib) of light from the mounts of the Hereafter. Others say: (p-513) they will be gathered as riders upon forms of their righteous deeds in the world, in the utmost beauty and fragrance.

Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his commentary on this noble verse: Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i, from Ibn Marzuq, concerning ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: The believer, when he comes out of his grave, will be met by the most beautiful form he has ever seen and the most fragrant of smells. He will say: "Who are you?" It will say: "Do you not recognize me?" He will say: "No, except that Allah has made your scent fragrant and your face beautiful." It will say: "I am your righteous deed. Likewise you were in the world, good and pure in deed. How often I have carried you in the world, so come, ride me." That is His saying: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: "Riders." Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ibn Mahdi narrated to me, from Sa'id, from Isma'il, from a man, from Abu Hurayrah: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, he said: "Upon camels." Ibn Jurayj said: "Upon swift she-camels." al-Thawri said: "Upon camels, she-camels." Qatadah said concerning ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾: "To Paradise." Abdullah ibn al-Imam Ahmad said in the Musnad of his father: Suwayd ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Ali ibn Musharhir informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, al-Nu'man ibn Sa'd narrated to us, who said: "We were sitting with Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and he recited this verse: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, and said: 'By Allah, they will not be gathered on their feet, nor will a delegation be gathered on their feet, but upon she-camels the like of which creation has never seen, upon which are saddles of gold, and they will ride them until they strike the gates of Paradise!!'" Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir also narrated this in the same way from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Madani, and he added: "Upon them are saddles of gold, and their reins are of chrysolite (zabarjad)." The rest is similar. Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated here a very strange hadith, marfu', from Ali, who said: My father narrated to us, Abu Ghassan Malik ibn Isma'il al-Nahdi narrated to us, Salamah ibn Ja'far al-Bajali narrated to us, I heard Abu Mu'adh al-Basri say: "Ali was one day with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and recited this verse: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing to the Most Merciful as a delegation﴾, and said: 'I do not think the wafd is anything but riders, O Messenger of Allah.' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they come out of their graves they will be met (or: they will be brought) with white she-camels that have wings, upon which are saddles of gold, the thongs of their sandals are a shining light, each step of which is as far as the eye can see. They will reach a tree from whose root two springs gush forth; they will drink from one of them, and it will wash what is in their bellies of impurity, and they will bathe in the other, and their skins and hair will never again become disheveled, and the radiance of bliss will flow over them. Then they will reach (or: come to) the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby (p-514) upon golden plates. They will strike the ring against the plate, and a resonance will be heard from it, O Ali. It will reach every maiden (hawra') that her husband has come, and she will send her keeper to open for him. When he sees him, she will fall prostrate to him (Salamah said: I think he said "prostrating"). He will say: "Raise your head, for I am only your keeper, appointed over your affair." He will follow him and tread in his footsteps, and the maiden will be hurried by eagerness, and she will come out from tents of pearls and rubies until she embraces him.'" ... to the end of the hadith in full. At the end of the chain: thus it occurs in this narration as marfu', but we have related it in the introductions from the words of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is more akin to authenticity, and Allah knows best. End of quotation.

Their riding mentioned here occurs only from the place of gathering to Paradise. As for from the grave, the apparent view is that they will be gathered on foot, based on the hadith of Ibn Abbas indicating that they will be gathered barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised. This is the apparent view, and al-Qurtubi affirmed it, and Allah the Exalted knows best.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿and drive the criminals to Hell like thirsty cattle﴾ [Maryam: 86]: driving (al-sawq) is well known. The criminals (al-mujrimun) is the sound plural of al-mujrim, which is the active participle of ijram (committing crime). Ijram is committing a jarimah, which is a sin for which its doer deserves punishment and torment. Ijram in the Qur'an comes only from the quadriliteral "ajram" on the pattern af'ala, though in the language it is permissible to use the triliteral form, so one says jarama yajrimu like daraba yadribu, and its active participle is jarim and its passive participle is majrum, as is evident. From it is the saying of Amr ibn al-Barraqah al-Nahmi:

"We support our master, knowing that he is, as with people, one who is wronged by him and one who wrongs."

His saying, exalted is He, in this noble verse: ﴿wirdan﴾, meaning thirsty (ʿiṭashan). The original meaning of wird is coming to water. Since coming to water only happens out of thirst, the term wird is used here for the group of thirsty ones. May Allah protect us and the Muslims from thirst in the Hereafter and in this world. And from the use of wird for going to water is the saying of the rajiz addressing his she-camel:

"Go on, go on, like the wird of a dumb dove, dusky-hued, whom the coolness of water has pleased."

The scholars differed about the governing element (al-'amil al-nasib) of His saying: ﴿On the Day We shall gather the God-fearing﴾. It was said it is governed by "yamlikuna" after it, meaning: they will not possess intercession on the Day We gather the God-fearing. Abu Hayyan chose this in al-Bahr. It was also said: it is governed by an implied "udhkur" (remember) or "ihdhar" (beware), and there are other opinions besides that.

What this noble verse contains is explained in other places, such as His saying, exalted is He, in Surat az-Zumar: (p-515) ﴿And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups, until when they reach it, its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this day of yours?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come true against the disbelievers."﴾ ﴿It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein. Wretched is the abode of the arrogant."﴾ ﴿And those who feared their Lord will be driven to Paradise in groups, until when they reach it, and its gates are opened, and its keepers say to them: "Peace be upon you; you have done well, so enter it, abiding forever."﴾ [az-Zumar: 71–73].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 96:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection﴾ [Maryam: 96], to the end of the verse.

We have already mentioned, in the introduction to this blessed book, that among the kinds of clarification (bayan) contained in it is that a general term (lafz 'amm) is mentioned in the Qur'an, and then in some places it is explicitly stated that some individuals of that general term are included in it. We have already given several examples of this. When you know this, then know that He, exalted is He, in this noble verse mentions that He will appoint for His believing servants who do righteous deeds affection (wudd), meaning love (mahabbah) in the hearts of His servants. In another place He has explicitly stated that His prophet Musa (peace be upon him), and our Prophet (prayers and peace be upon him), are included in this generality, namely in His saying: ﴿And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾ [Ta-Ha: 39], to the end of the verse. And in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh), from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "When Allah loves a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'O Jibril, I love so-and-so, so love him.' He said: So Jibril loves him. Then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah loves so-and-so, so love him.' He said: So the inhabitants of the heavens love him. Then acceptance (al-qabul) is placed for him on the earth. And when Allah hates a servant, He calls Jibril and says: 'O Jibril, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: So Jibril hates him. (p-518) Then he calls out among the inhabitants of the heavens: 'Indeed Allah hates so-and-so, so hate him.' He said: So the inhabitants of the heavens hate him. Then enmity (al-baghda') is placed for him on the earth." End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 19, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue, that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people contentious.﴾

In this noble verse, Exalted and Majestic is He mentions that He has only made this Qur'an easy upon the tongue of this noble Arab Prophet, so that he may give good tidings thereby to the righteous (al-muttaqin), and warn thereby the fierce adversaries (al-khusum al-aladda'), who are the disbelievers. What this verse contains has been clarified in other places. As for what it mentions of the facilitation of this mighty Qur'an, He has explained it in other places, such as:

• His saying in surah "al-Qamar", repeating it: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ [al-Qamar: 32],

• and His saying at the end of "al-Dukhan": ﴿So We have only made it easy in your tongue, that they may remember.﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58]. As for what it mentions of it being in the tongue of this noble Arab Prophet, He has mentioned it in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And indeed, it is a revelation from the Lord of the worlds. The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down, upon your heart, that you may be among the warners, in a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 192-195],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book. Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.﴾ [Yusuf: 1-2],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ha, Mim. By the clear Book. Indeed, We have made it an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 1-3],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ [al-Nahl: 103],

and other verses besides these.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous﴾, and so on, we have already clarified the verses indicating it in surah "al-Kahf" and elsewhere, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it here. The most apparent of the opinions regarding His saying "ludda" is that it is the plural of "alad", meaning one of intense enmity. From it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he is the most vehement of adversaries﴾ [al-Baqarah: 204], and the saying of the poet:

I pass the night in private conversation with worries, as if I were disputing with people who are contentious in argument, quarrelsome.

"And how many generations have We destroyed before them? Do you perceive any one of them, or hear from them a whisper?" [Qur'an 19:98]

"Kam" (how many) in this noble verse is the khabariyyah (the "kam" used for numerical assertion), and it is in the accusative position, because it is the object of "ahlakna" (We destroyed). And "min" is the explanatory "min" that clarifies "kam", as its explanation has already passed.

His saying: "Hal tuhissu minhum min ahad" means: do you see any one of them, or feel of him, or find him? "Aw tasma'u lahum rikzan" means: a sound. The root of "rikz" is a faint sound. From it comes "rakkaza al-rumh" (he planted the spear), when he hid its tip and buried it in the ground. From it also comes "al-rikaz", which is a pre-Islamic buried treasure hidden under the earth. As for the use of "rikz" to mean a sound, there is the saying of Labid in his Mu'allaqah:

"So she sensed the rikz of a companion, and alarm seized her, from a hidden place, while the companion was her sickness."

And the saying of Tarafah in his Mu'allaqah:

"And two ears that are alert to hearing the night's travel, to a faint rikz or to a sound that is clearly heard."

And the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"When a deserted, wary wild ass senses a rikz, with a sound's alert, nothing in its hearing is false."

The interrogative in his saying "hal" is meant for negation, and the meaning is: We destroyed many of the past nations, so you do not see any one of them, nor do you hear any sound from them. What he mentions in this verse of the non-sighting of their persons and the non-hearing of their voices, he has mentioned some of it in other places, such as:

- His saying about 'Ad: "So do you see any remnant of them?" [al-Haqqah: 8]
- His saying about them: "So they were not seen except for their dwellings" [al-Ahqaf: 25]
- His saying: "And how many a city We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so it is fallen upon its roofs, and an abandoned well, and a lofty palace." [al-Hajj: 45]

And to other verses besides these.
